we propose an on-the-fly approximation algorithm for the multivariate Total Variation problem, and show its efficiency in a variety of applications.
we propose an efficient algorithm for multivariate change-point analysis, based on the local validation on the Karush-Kun-Tucker conditions of the dual problem.

we propose a multivariate change-point on-the-fly algorithm, that we show that the non-local setting prevents from obtaining an exact on-the-flow solution, and that we provide a practitioner-tunable trade-off parameter to control the quality of the solution, while benefiting from computational costs orders of magnitudes lower than standard iterative algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and the analysis of efficient algorithms for change-point detection in the context of multivariate data, and with the assessment of their performances.
the design of efficient on-the-fly strategies to detect changes in multivariate signals.
a new algorithm for change-point detection in multivariate data.

we have developed an on-the-fly multivariate change-point algorithm, whose performance is comparable to that of the state-of-the-art algorithms, while providing a significant computational advantage.

we have designed and implemented an on-the-fly multivariate change-point algorithm, whose performance is comparable with state-of-the-art iterative algorithms, while being computationally orders of magnitude faster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the multivariate setting, on-the-fly strategies are not necessarily doomed to fail.
, in the multivariate setting, an on-the-fly procedure can be obtained by relaxing the exactness of the solution, which is not the case in the univariate setting.

, by exploiting the structure of the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, we can devise a multivariate on-the-fly algorithm, whose computational cost can be tuned, and that can provide a good quality approximate solution.
